title: Match interventions to defaults with Jev and propose versioned defaults
summary: Add a defaults-learning step: for each recorded user intervention or correction, ask Jev (through a trait with a fake, behind the Vercel AI Gateway HTTP API) which existing default it matches. When the same unmatched correction repeats past a threshold, produce a proposed new default and a version bump as a reviewable proposal. The step never edits defaults.toml itself.

defaults_applied.how: Use an existing HTTP client crate for the gateway call and record the call.
New module has tests using a fake Jev; cargo test and clippy pass.
Add a short decisions entry with alternatives before or with the build.
Version bump and duplicate-id checks are enforced in code by DefaultsModel::parse.
No credentials or personal data in files or output.
One focused matching and proposal step, with no auto-apply.
Hidden requirements (the threshold, the proposal format) are inferred from the repository and the brief.

assumptions: Jev is the typesafe-ai/jev model reached through the Vercel AI Gateway HTTP API, per BRIEF.md. D31 excluded it from v0, so this job reintroduces it narrowly.

Interventions and corrections come from existing job and outcome records, such as user intervention flags and verifier findings. Records are not visible to me, so the input type is read from athena-data records.
Proposals are reviewed by the user and not auto-applied, because defaults.toml is governance and the designed default requires review.
question: Should proposals only be written for review, or may Athena land a new defaults.toml version on its own? I assumed review only.

acceptance_criteria.text: A decision-log entry in docs/decisions.md records the design: a Jev matching step, the alternatives considered, and the reversal of D31's exclusion of Jev, scoped to this decision type. Its use of Jev is shadowed or labeled until calibrated.
Jev is reached only through a trait with a deterministic fake. The gateway credential is read from the environment and never written to files, records or output.

A matcher takes an intervention or correction record plus the defaults model and returns either a matched default id with a probability, or no match. Low-confidence results are flagged for escalation.

A repeat rule (a stated threshold on unmatched corrections that cluster together) yields a proposed default with id, statement, applies_to and a source citing the intervention records. It also yields a bumped version number.
defaults.toml is not modified by the step. Proposals are written as output for review, and DefaultsModel::parse still validates the result.
cargo test passes with new unit tests that use the fake Jev. They cover a match, no match, a repeat that crosses the threshold, a repeat that stays below it, and a duplicate id being rejected.
cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check are clean.

out_of_scope: Editing defaults.toml directly or auto-landing new defaults
Jev as a forecaster or routing tier
departures: The request is broad: it introduces a new external model dependency, which D31 had excluded, and a new design. I raised cost and time above the reference and lowered acceptance and verification pass.
